verdict.rationale: Stripe Treasury documents Transaction objects as the ledger entry for every movement of funds. The docs position them for building activity feeds and reconciliation, with transaction-created events and separate flow objects such as ReceivedDebit, so the core building block is first-party. Nothing in the pack shows how rich that data is. missing for 10: documented counterparty details, rail-specific metadata (ACH/wire fields), explicit stable-identifier guarantees, merchant/category enrichment, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, transaction data is rich enough to build on — counterparty details, rail-specific metadata, stable identifiers, and enrichment that makes a raw bank feed usable in-product

citations.quote: Every movement of funds into or out of a financial account creates a Transaction object. Transactions are the ledger entries for your financial accounts.
Use transactions to build account activity feeds, reconcile against your internal systems, and track money movement through your platform.
Any transaction initiated after this authorization generates a ReceivedDebit object
